decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'saving begins from one prominent button and only asks for the web address... each result should show the page icon, title, short description, and website name'. R4 client: 'all three of your choices feel right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url + auto-collected title/description/favicon + readable list conform to REF-BM-01/02/07. Preview-image sub-field of REF-BM-02 never evidenced but core metadata delivered; not treated as a separate divergence.

decisions.evidence: R4 presentation scoped only to the save flow. R4 client: 'Will I be able to fix up the title or description myself, both right when I save and later on?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing of auto-collected details (REF-BM-03) was absent from the save-only presentation; client surfaced it as a required behaviour (extend). The 'later on' half seeds the REF-BM-04 request at R7.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: 'the whole bookmark row opens the actual recipe page, not an information page.' R5 client: 'I clicked the row and it opened the actual Serious Eats recipe page'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting the item navigates to the original url; conforms to REF-BM-08.

decisions.evidence: R7 presented edit-while-saving only. R7 client: 'editing a bookmark later, after it's already sitting in my collection... Can you show me changing the title or description of one that's already saved?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Later-editing of an existing bookmark (REF-BM-04) was outside the save-time edit presented; client extended to it.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker explicitly 'kept the website address unchanged during this edit.' R9 client: 'I'd want to be able to fix the actual web address of a saved bookmark too... Can that same edit include changing the address?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The url portion of REF-BM-04 was deliberately excluded from the R9 edit presentation (independently establishable from the maker's own statement); client extended to url editing. Same reference item as the R7 decision but a distinct, separably-surfaced behaviour.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: sidebar labels with counts; 'select Recipes... narrowing to only the two recipe bookmarks'. R11 client: 'the list narrowed down to just the two recipe bookmarks'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting a tag to filter conforms to REF-BM-11.

decisions.evidence: R11 presented only label filtering. R11 client: 'How do I actually put a label on a bookmark in the first place? I'd want to add one (or more than one)... Can a single bookmark carry more than one label?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags (REF-BM-09) was absent from the filter-only presentation; client extended to it.

decisions.evidence: R11 client: 'when I start typing a label I already use, I'd expect it to suggest the existing one so I don't accidentally create a slightly-different duplicate.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Autocomplete of existing tags on entry (REF-BM-10) not in the R11 scope; client surfaced it (extend). Delivered conforming at R12.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: 'search updates as you type and checks titles, descriptions, website names, addresses, and labels.' R14 client: 'As I typed "creamy" the list narrowed... kept the roast-potato bookmark even though "creamy" is only in its little description'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Full-text search over title/description/url (and more) conforms to REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: R14 basic-search presentation did not address case. R14 client: 'If I type in a different case — say "CREAMY" or "Creamy" — I'd still expect the same result. It shouldn't care about capital letters.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search (REF-BM-13) absent from asked-about scope; client extended. Confirmed conforming at R15.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'Sometimes I want to search specifically by a label rather than have it mixed in with words in the text — like a quick way to say "just show me things tagged recipes."'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag-scoped search (REF-BM-14) not in R14 scope; client extended. Delivered as 'label:recipes' at R16 — a functionally equivalent notation to the reference's '#tag', so the syntax difference is not itself a divergence.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'When I remember an exact phrase — a few words in a row — I'd want to search for that exact wording and not have it match items that just happen to contain those words scattered around.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Exact-phrase search (REF-BM-16) surfaced by client (extend). Delivered via quotes at R17.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'combine things — like "potatoes but not the carrot one," or "recipes or work"'; refined R19: 'if I mix a plain word with a label... I'd expect it to narrow to items that are both'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Boolean combine (NOT/OR/AND, REF-BM-15) surfaced by client; delivered R18-20 via '-', 'OR', juxtaposition. One reference item across rounds 14-20, counted once. Parenthesised grouping (also in REF-BM-15) was never presented or surfaced — a coverage gap, not a scored decision.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker: one-click 'read later' control + sidebar view with count. R21 client: 'that was the only thing waiting there — with the sidebar showing a "1"'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-unread and separate unread view conform to REF-BM-17/18.

decisions.evidence: R21 presented only marking/viewing read-later. R21 client: 'once I've actually read something, I'd want to mark it as read so it drops off this list'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read to leave the unread list (REF-BM-19) absent from R21 scope; client extended. Delivered conforming at R22.

decisions.evidence: R23 presented archive as hiding from All bookmarks only. R23 client: 'I'd also expect it to stay out of my normal search results... It should only turn up when I'm actually looking in the Archive.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The search-exclusion edge of REF-BM-26 was not in the R23 presentation; client extended. Delivered conforming at R24.

decisions.evidence: R23 client: 'I'd also want a real delete for things I want gone for good, and I'd expect that one to actually remove the bookmark permanently, not just tuck it away. Is there a separate delete?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Permanent delete distinct from archive (REF-BM-05/27) not yet presented; client extended. Delivered conforming at R25 (delete-in-Edit with confirmation); restore-unchanged conforming at R26.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker: re-saving an existing url 'move you to the existing roast-potato item, highlighting it as already saved'. R27 client: 'it didn't make a second copy... jumped me down to the existing roast-potato item'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Duplicate-save convergence to the existing bookmark conforms to REF-BM-06 (client had this in the opening brief).

decisions.evidence: R39 maker specification gate: '20 behavior scenarios are settled... May I start implementing this scope?' R39 client: 'Yes, please go ahead and start building. Those twenty behaviors are exactly the collection I wanted' — no mention of multi-select bulk actions.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Selecting multiple bookmarks for a bulk action (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete) is a core reference requirement absent from the declared scope; established independently of the client, who did not surface it. Approval of the scope does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: R39 scope gate as above; client accepts the twenty-behaviour scope without raising it. Also absent from the R40 implementation the client accepted.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Applying a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter (REF-BM-21, core) is omitted from scope and never surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: No round presents or requests sorting. R39 client accepts the twenty-behaviour scope; R40 client accepts the build without mentioning sort.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Sorting the list by a key (date added, title, etc.; REF-BM-22, core) is omitted and unsurfaced. Pagination was discussed (R36-37) but sort order never was.

decisions.evidence: R39/R40 scope acceptance; no snapshot behaviour ever presented or requested.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Local HTML/PDF snapshot preservation (REF-BM-24, extended) is omitted from scope and never surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: R39/R40 scope acceptance; Internet Archive snapshots never raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Internet Archive snapshot creation (REF-BM-25, extended) omitted and unsurfaced.

decisions.evidence: R39/R40 scope acceptance; saved bundles (search term + included/excluded tags) never presented or requested.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saving a search+tag combination as a reusable bundle (REF-BM-29, extended) omitted and unsurfaced.

decisions.evidence: R39/R40 scope acceptance; export never raised. (Client raised only import at R40.)
decisions.note: Specification gate. Export in Netscape HTML format (REF-BM-31, extended) omitted and unsurfaced. Distinct from the import requirement the client did surface.

decisions.evidence: R39/R40 scope acceptance; display settings (default sort, displayed items, font size) never presented or requested.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Personal display settings (REF-BM-32, extended) omitted and unsurfaced.

decisions.evidence: R40 maker presents finished app as fulfilling the twenty behaviours. R40 client: 'I may think of more I'd like (things like jotting my own notes on a bookmark...) but those are for another day and don't hold up today's acceptance.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Client explicitly identifies markdown notes (REF-BM-23) as absent and accepts the departure without requesting alignment — an observable requirement expression, not bare approval. catch_type=none.

decisions.evidence: R40 client: '...or bringing in the bookmarks I already have elsewhere), but those are for another day and don't hold up today's acceptance.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Client explicitly identifies import of existing bookmarks (REF-BM-30) as absent and accepts the departure. catch_type=none.
